dataNotes: Whyte's own two-page PDF spec sheet for SKU W629(size)V6. MODEL YEAR VERIFIED: the whytebikes.com/products/629-my24 page carries SKU 'W6292MV6', tying MY24 to the V6 sheet. STATED: material ('6061 alloy, hydroformed T6, multi-butted'); BB ('BSA, 73mm'); rear axle ('12mm x 148mm Boost dropouts'); brake mount ('chainstay Post Mount (PM) dropouts' - native rotor size never stated, so generic POST_MOUNT rather than POST_MOUNT_160/180); wheel ('TRAIL HARDTAIL 29ER'); max tyre ('29 x 2.5 Rear' = 63.5mm, rounded DOWN to 63 so clearance is never overstated); max chainring 34T; chainstay 450mm all sizes; seatpost 30.9mm all sizes. DERIVED: headsetTaper (tapered head tube plus 'FSA No.57B Orbit ZS, 1 1/2in lower, 1 1/8in upper'); dropoutType from '12mm x 148mm Boost dropouts'; hangerStandard PROPRIETARY - 'Dropout Part Code DROPWH17' is a Whyte part number, and the same field on Whyte's T-160 V3 sheet reads 'SRAM UDH', proving the field denotes hanger standard, so DROPWH17 is definitively not UDH. LEFT NULL: maxRotorMmRear (only stock 180mm listed, no maximum); maxForkTravelMm (stock 120mm fork only); bottleMounts (not mentioned); iscgStandard (the 'ISG Chain Guide' row is BLANK and 'Chain Guide Part Code' reads N/A - blank is not a stated NONE); mulletApproved, hasEyelets (not addressed; null rather than guessing false). SCOPE: the V5 sheet shows byte-identical geometry and wording so it is almost certainly the same mould, but its model year could not be verified and it states a smaller rear clearance (2.4in), so V5 is deliberately excluded rather than have a year guessed.

MODEL-YEAR TRAP EXPLICITLY HANDLED: a DIFFERENT frame platform from the pre-2026 Mythique 29, not a respec. Vitus's generic mythique-29-geometry page STILL SERVES THE OLD generation's data, so relying on it for a current bike would have written wrong hanger and shock specs. The 2026 frame changes four hard standards: hanger (UDH vs non-UDH), shock (185mm vs 200mm eye-to-eye), chain device (ISCG 05 vs None) and BB drop. Year STATED on-page. This page is internally CONSISTENT - frame line, component list and geometry table agree on axle, shock and tyre - which is why it is trusted, unlike the 2026 Sentier/Nucleus pages which contradict themselves. STATED: material ('Mythique 6061-T6 Alloy'); BB ('73mm BSA'); axle ('148mm x 12mm UDH, 181mm length, M12xP1.0'); hanger UDH (stated twice); brake mount ('post mount', base rotor size not stated so generic POST_MOUNT); max rotor 200mm; headset ('ZS44/28.6 upper and ZS56/40 lower to suit 1-1/8in upper tapered to 1.5in lower' - stated in words, not inferred); max tyre ('29 x 2.5' = 63.5mm, rounded DOWN to 63); max chainring 32T; chainstay 445mm; seatpost 31.6mm; ISCG 05 all sizes; shock eye-to-eye 185mm. LEFT NULL: shockStrokeMm - the frame legitimately takes TWO strokes ('S: 185x50 (130mm travel)' and 'L: 185x55 (141mm travel)'), so no single platform-level value is correct; shockMountType (trunnion vs eyelet never stated); maxForkTravelMm; bottleMounts; mulletApproved. NOTE: chainstay 445mm coincidentally matches the older generation; every other standard differs, so this is not evidence of a shared mould.

The PRE-2026 Mythique 29 mould - distinct from the 2026 UDH frame (200mm vs 185mm shock, no UDH, no ISCG). Confirmed across three Vitus pages that agree on frame standards. Confidence medium ONLY because Vitus contradict themselves on the shock; every required field is solid. STATED: material ('6061-T6'); BB ('73mm BSA', all sizes); axle ('148mm x 12mm thru axle'); brake mount ('post mount disc brake mounts'); wheel 29in; max tyre (frame-clearance row '29 x 2.5' = 63.5mm, rounded DOWN to 63); chainstay 445mm; seatpost 31.6mm; shock eye-to-eye 200mm. DERIVED: headsetTaper ('ZS44/28.6 - ZS56/40'; ZS56/40 is by definition a 1.5in lower race); dropoutType from 'thru axle'; iscgStandard NONE ('Chain Device: None' consistently across all sizes, in the same table as BB/headset/axle, so a frame-standard statement not a build omission). LEFT NULL: shockStrokeMm - THREE conflicting manufacturer figures (200x51, 200x56, and 'S: 200x51; L: 200x57'); shockMountType - DIRECT CONTRADICTION between two Vitus pages, one says 'trunnion', the other describes '22.2x8mm hardware both ends' which is a standard eyelet. The hardware description looks more credible but a manufacturer page says otherwise, so abstained rather than risk excluding legal shocks. WORTH A HUMAN RESOLVING. Also null: maxRotorMmRear, maxForkTravelMm, maxChainringTeeth, bottleMounts, hangerStandard (never stated), mulletApproved. YEAR CAVEAT: 2022 comes from Vitus's own product URL slug and collection grouping, NOT an on-page year statement. Vitus's geometry footnote confirms VR/VRW (130mm) and VRS/VRX (140mm) share this one frame; specs were verified on the VRS pages, so only VRS is listed.

Separate mould from the Mythique 29 - different wheel size and 435mm vs 445mm chainstay, confirmed on Vitus's own geometry tables. STATED: material ('6061-T6 double butted'); BB ('73mm BSA', all sizes); axle ('148mm x 12mm thru axle'); brake mount ('post mount disc brake mounts'); wheel 27.5in; max tyre ('27.5 x 2.6' = 66.04mm -> 66); chainstay 435mm; seatpost 31.6mm; shock eye-to-eye 200mm. DERIVED: headsetTaper ('ZS44/28.6 - ZS56/40'); dropoutType from 'thru axle'. LEFT NULL: iscgStandard - Vitus's own Chain Device row is SELF-CONTRADICTORY across sizes ('None' for S/M/L but 'ISCG 05' for XL, on the same table, on both pages), so abstained rather than pick one; shockStrokeMm (conflicting 200x51 / 200x56 / 'S: 200x51; L: 200x57'); shockMountType (same trunnion vs '22.2x8mm hardware both ends' contradiction as the 29in frame); maxRotorMmRear, maxForkTravelMm, maxChainringTeeth, bottleMounts, hangerStandard, mulletApproved. YEAR CAVEAT: 2022 from Vitus's product URL slug and collection grouping, not an on-page statement.

GENERATION SCOPE: the redesigned Lux Trail launched via Canyon's own newsroom, 140mm front / 125mm rear, frame 1,850g. All four en-gb product pages carry Year = 2027 in their embedded product data, so the model year of the pages read matches the generation described in the press release - no MY ambiguity. Does NOT cover the previous Lux Trail (frame code M084, PressFit 92 per Canyon's own BB support article), which is a different platform. STATED: material ('Material Carbon (CF)', frame 1850g); BB ('Bottom bracket standard BSA 73'); axle ('Axle dimension 12x148 mm', 'Thru Axle Canyon Quixle'); wheel ('Wheel Size 29"' every size XS-XL); max tyre ('Frame tyre clearance = 2,40"' on CF 6/7/8/9 = 61mm - note fork clearance is listed separately as 69mm, that is the fork not the frame); chainstay 435mm on XS/S/M (440mm on L/XL - SIZE-DEPENDENT, 435 recorded as the majority value); seatpost 31.6mm all sizes; shock ('Fitting Length 210X55' every size, consistent across CF 6/7/8/9). DERIVED: dropoutType and hangerStandard UDH - Canyon does not print 'UDH' on these pages, but CF 7 ships SRAM Eagle 90 Transmission and CF 8/9 ship GX/X0 Eagle AXS Transmission (all stated), and SRAM T-Type derailleurs mount only to a UDH-compatible dropout. That is a hard mechanical requirement rather than a class assumption, but it is inference not a Canyon statement. headsetTaper DERIVED from the OE fork's stated 'Fork steer tube diameter 1 1/8" - 1,5"'. rearBrakeMountType DERIVED from Canyon's newsroom stating 'an isolated post-mount brake adapter allows the seatstays to flex unrestricted' - confirms post-mount but not the base tab size, so unsized POST_MOUNT. This is the weakest field and the reason confidence is medium. LEFT NULL: maxRotorMmRear (180mm is the fitted rotor, no frame maximum stated); mulletApproved (no mullet option or flip chip, and no statement either way - not treated as a confirmed false); maxForkTravelMm (140mm is the fitted fork, no frame maximum); maxChainringTeeth (32T fitted, no maximum); bottleMounts; iscgStandard (nothing stated for Lux Trail; Canyon do list an ISCG05 plate for the Spectral CF but nothing is carried across); shockMountType.
